rationale: The `Test-removed:` trailer is the right instrument and this is NOT the inversion testing.md rule 4 exists to catch. Decisive evidence, all of it in the tree and predating the commit: the M4.4b backlog row as it stood at HEAD already required 'reserve 0 for no lease and start the first term at 1 (a change to LeaseManager AND ITS TEST)'. The specification pre-authorised the test change, in writing, before the production edit. Verified independently: (a) both new tests carry red records in .harness/tdd/red.json (1788400998, 1788401000) and check-tdd prints 'ok 2 new test(s), all observed failing first'; (b) the replacement assertion is equal-or-stricter -- isZero() and isEqualTo(1) both pin exactly one value, but isEqualTo(1) additionally kills the constant-return-0/default-value mutation class that isZero() passed, and I killed it: reverting the cold start to new Lease(0,...) fails theFirstAcquisitionStartsAtEpochOneBecauseZeroMeansNoLease along with five others; (c) the author's claim about the gate is correct -- scripts/test_integrity.py STRENGTH scores isZero, isNotZero and isEqualTo all at weight 3, so an in-place edit keeping the old name would have scored 0 -> 0 and flagged NOTHING. The rename raised a louder flag than the quieter alternative, which is the opposite of gaming the gate. Suite verified independently: 491 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped. No assertion anywhere in the diff was weakened: every changed assertion is an exact-value pin shifted by the spec change (0->1, 1->2), and the remaining edits are .as() descriptions and comments only.

findings.title: noAcquisitionEverWritesEpochZero... does not test the one input that can falsify its own universal: an existing lease object AT epoch 0
findings.failure_scenario: SURVIVING MUTATION, verified by running the full suite: change Lease.takenOverBy from `new Lease(epoch + 1, ...)` to `new Lease(epoch == 0 ? 0 : epoch + 1, ...)` -- i.e. a takeover of an epoch-0 lease ADOPTS epoch 0 instead of bumping to 1. All 491 tests pass. That mutation writes a LEASE at epoch 0, which is precisely the state this whole commit exists to make impossible, and the test whose name says 'NO acquisition path EVER writes epoch zero' does not see it. The reason is that no test anywhere in the tree ever feeds takenOverBy a lease at epoch 0: LeaseTest#takingOverBumpsTheEpochByExactlyOneAndReplacesTheHolder starts at epoch 4, and both LeaseManager takeover tests start from a lease this commit just made start at 1. The input is not hypothetical -- Lease.java's new javadoc in THIS diff deliberately keeps 0 parseable ('decode must still parse a legacy or hand-edited object'), and the pre-M4.4b build of this very class minted exactly such an object on every cold start, so a rolling upgrade presents it. Production is CORRECT on this path (epoch+1 from 0 is 1); the gap is in the tests. Verified red/green: adding a test that puts `new Lease(0, "podA", "", clock.millis()).encode()` into the store, calls tryAcquire, and asserts `isEqualTo(1)` FAILS under the mutation and PASSES against the staged production code. Three lines, and it is the only assertion in the suite that would make the test's name true. Suggest it here or as a line on M4.6, which already owns the unleased-chain obligation.

findings.title: The new test is dominated -- it kills a strict subset of what the exact-value tests beside it already kill
findings.failure_scenario: Its three assertions (isNotZero, isNotZero, isGreaterThan) are strictly weaker restatements of values two neighbouring tests already pin exactly. Measured: mutate the cold start to `new Lease(5, podId, endpoint, ...)`. Five tests fail -- theFirstAcquisitionStartsAtEpochOne..., anExpiredLeaseIsTakenOver..., theHolderRenewsWithoutChangingTheEpoch, releaseKeepsTheEpoch..., aHolderCanRenewRepeatedly... -- and noAcquisitionEverWritesEpochZero... PASSES, because 5 is not zero and 6 > 5. Conversely every mutation that DOES kill it (cold start -> 0, takeover -> 0) also kills at least two exact-value tests, so it is never the sole killer. Net effect on the suite's discriminating power today: zero. It is documentation with an assertion attached, which is not worthless, but it does establish isNotZero() as the named assertion for the project's central fencing invariant -- and test_integrity.py scores isNotZero at the same weight 3 as isEqualTo, so a future relaxation of the exact pins down to this weaker form would pass the gate silently. Closing finding 1 (the epoch-0-source takeover input) is what would give this test a kill nothing else has and make it earn its place.

findings.title: The row's claim about the Test-removed: trailer is a promise about a commit body that does not exist yet
findings.failure_scenario: The row states 'Declared with the gate's own Test-removed: trailer rather than worked around'. I verified the gate's behaviour -- test_integrity.py downgrades the removal FAIL to WARN only when the body matches ^Test-removed:\s*\S -- and I verified the gate currently FAILS on the staged bytes with no message file. But the trailer itself is unverifiable at review time, since nothing is committed. If the commit is made with SKIP=check-test-integrity, or with --no-verify, or with the trailer misspelled, the row asserts something that never happened and nothing downstream will notice (AGENTS.md is explicit that this is a local-only gate). Every other claim in the row I could check IS honest: DefaultIngest is the sole production `new CommitLog(store, prefix)` call site so the colliding writer really was production, not hypothetical; the FORK price is carried onto M4.6 (remove the unleased commit path, not merely pass an epoch) and onto M4.5 (CONTINUE may not use prevEpoch=0 as an absent-sentinel), matching the production reviewer's finding; and '491 tests green' is exact -- I counted 491/0/0/0 from the JUnit XML myself.
